chunks: As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from al-Ḥasan, from Zurʿah, from Samāʿah, who said:

I asked him about the hand, and he said: “Half of the diyah. And for the ear, half of the diyah if it is cut off from its root; and if he cuts off a part of it, then an equitable valuation. And for one eye, half of the diyah. And for the nose, if the soft protruding part is cut off, the full diyah. And for the male organ, if it is cut off, the full diyah. And the two lips, the upper and the lower, are equal regarding the diyah.”

So a possible way to understand the equality between the two lips in the diyah in this report is that what is intended is the imposition of diyah upon both equally, not the amount; thus they are equal in the sense that diyah is due for each one of them, even if they differ in the amount that is deserved for each of them.

key_terms.الدِّيَةِ: financial compensation due for bodily injury
key_terms.الذَّكَرِ: the male organ, whose severance carries the full diyah
key_terms.الشَّفَتَانِ: the two lips, discussed as equal with respect to diyah liability
key_terms.الْأُذُنِ: the ear, whose full removal from the root carries half of the diyah
key_terms.الْعَيْنِ الْوَاحِدَةِ: one eye, for which half of the diyah is due
key_terms.الْمَارِنُ: the soft projecting part of the nose
key_terms.الْيَدِ: the hand, for which half of the diyah is stated
key_terms.قِيمَةُ عَدْلٍ: an equitable assessed value for partial injury

ai.seo_question: What diyah is due in Shia fiqh for cutting the hand, ear, eye, nose, male organ, or lips?
ai.summary: This report sets out legal rulings concerning diyah for injuries to specific body parts, including the hand, ear, eye, nose, male organ, and lips. It also clarifies that the statement about the two lips being equal in diyah may refer to the principle that compensation applies to both, not necessarily that the exact amount is identical in every case.
